The venue change follows the WTA’s decision to end its three-year hosting agreement with Riyadh a year early, reportedly due to concerns over the war in the Middle East. bullets: Betfred has ended its sponsorship of horseracing's five British Classics, covering the 1000 and 2000 Guineas at Newmarket, the Derby and Oaks at Epsom, and the St Leger at Doncaster. The gambling firm said it had "no choice" but to walk away from its partnerships with the Jockey Club and Arena Racing Company after the latest Budget raised machine games duty from 20% to 25%, a rise it said could put 1,420 jobs at risk.

The decision comes three years after Betfred took over the Derby, Oaks and St Leger in 2023, and added the Guineas races from 2025. It follows Betfred's announcement that it will end its Super League title sponsorship after the 2026 season, and its decision to let its British Masters golf deal lapse. The Jockey Club's Amy Starkey said the organisation understood the reasons and is in talks with several prospective replacement partners.

LFP Media chief executive Olivier Bramly said the reserve price was "ambitious" but a "bargain" for the winner.

Changes to French regulations allow the LFP to offer all matches as a single bundle. Bidders can seek either the rights to all matches, which would close Ligue 1+, or exclusive distribution rights for the service. Mediapro bid €814m a year in 2018, and DAZN and BeIN Sports signed €500m-a-year deals in 2024 before DAZN ended its contract early. Japanese technology group NTT will join the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team from the 2027 season, on a multi-year agreement focused on artificial intelligence security. NTT will help the team with its aim of becoming the most AI-fluent team on the grid, with AI security governance central to the work. Its role includes supporting the framework McLaren uses to manage security risks arising from its use of AI, and helping the team adopt the technology responsibly. NTT will also run a global engagement programme for clients and fans, using the partnership to show how its technology supports McLaren on and off the track.

The work will be delivered with the team at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, the base of a British team that won back-to-back Constructors’ Championships in 2024 and 2025 and took the 2025 Drivers’ title with Lando Norris. In 2025, McLaren won its first Drivers’ title since 2008. This season, under F1’s new technical regulations, the team is third in the Constructors’ standings behind Mercedes and Ferrari.

The Court of Auditors of the State of Minas Gerais (TCEMG) has suspended, in a precautionary decision, the sports sponsorship contracts worth R$ 32 million planned for 2027 between Minas Gerais state-owned companies and the clubs Cruzeiro, Atlético-MG and América-MG. The measure, signed this Tuesday (November 3rd) by acting councilor Licurgo Mourão, prevents the formalization of new agreements and orders the suspension of payments if contracts have already been signed.

The decision responds to Representation 1.220.989, presented by Senator and Governor-elect Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicans). In his statements, Cleitinho classified the sponsorship as "electioneering" and questioned the priority of the measure given the state's financial difficulties. Wider Sports News.copy:
Nielsen’s 2026 Annual Marketing Report shows Indian marketers leading six markets in planned spending increases on sponsorship and event media. The survey also finds India ahead on viewing sports sponsorship as a way to test new audiences, even as measurement of returns remains weak.

Indian brands are preparing to lean harder into live experiences, sports properties and creator-led marketing, even as many still struggle to track whether those bets pay off. Nielsen’s 2026 Annual Marketing Report, cited by Business Standard, suggests India is emerging as the most aggressive market among six surveyed when it comes to sponsorship and event media spending plans.India expect to raise spending on sponsorship and event media over the next 12 to 24 months. That is the highest share among the six markets studied and points to a broader shift in how brands are thinking about reach, relevance and audience discovery. The survey covered 1,200 marketers in India, the US, the UK, Italy, France and Germany, with 200 respondents from each market.Live events are moving up the marketing agendaNielsen data is not just higher spending intent, but where that money is likely to go. The company’s survey measured sponsorship and event media as a wider category that includes sporting as well as cultural events, so the findings reflect a broader appetite for live audience engagement rather than only sports-specific deals. Even so, sports remains central to the conversation because of its scale, fan loyalty and ability to deliver repeated exposure across platforms.India sees sports as a testing groundsports sponsorship itself. A majority of respondents in India, 61 per cent, said sports sponsorship serves as a way to test new audiences and markets. That was ahead of the US at 54 per cent and Germany at 32 per cent, suggesting Indian brands are increasingly treating sports not only as a reach tool but also as a laboratory for audience experimentation.Spending is rising, but measurement still lagsCreator-led marketing is reinforcing the shiftcreator content. Nielsen found that 81 per cent of Indian marketers rated influencer and creator content as very or extremely effective, compared with 54 per cent in the US. Rugby.title: Borthwick gets a glimpse of first-choice back three – before injuries strike again
Rugby.summary: Borthwick gets a glimpse of first-choice back three – before injuries strike again The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Rugby, at its heart, is a simple game. Win the collisions and you’ll more than likely win the match. Rule the skies, own the floor and the chances are you’ll end up on the right side of the ledger. Put square pegs in square holes and you can achieve the sort of attacking fluidity required for a record score against Australia. The complicated bit, once you stop trying to put them in round holes, is keeping those square pegs fit.

England’s emphatic win against the Wallabies on Sunday was the first time in two years Borthwick has been able to field a back three of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank. It was also the first time they have lined up with 11, 14 and 15 on their respective backs.

The injury came in a hip-drop tackle by Angus Bell, who received a yellow card, and Henry Pollock replaced him after half-time. The 23-year-old missed the 2025 Six Nations after shoulder surgery and this year's edition with a hamstring injury.

Seb Atkinson, Ollie Chessum and George Furbank are also out of Saturday's match against Japan, and flanker Tom Curry will miss the autumn with hip discomfort. Max Hicks and Jack Kenningham have been called into the 36-man squad. England then face New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday 21 November, with finals weekend on 27-29 November.

England will also be without a handful of other key players for the match against Japan on Saturday, with Seb Atkinson, forward Ollie Chessum and full-back George Furbank all ruled out.

bullets: Argentina and Toulouse utility back Juan Cruz Mallia faces a potentially lengthy absence after a fresh injury to his right knee during the Pumas' defeat to Ireland in Dublin on Friday night. The 30-year-old, who underwent surgery less than a year ago for an anterior cruciate ligament rupture, was hit late by Ireland lock James Ryan. According to Le Figaro, he has returned to Toulouse for further medical examinations.

He had previously ruptured his ACL after a late tackle by Tom Curry in a 27-23 loss to England in the 2025 Autumn Nations Series. Toulouse's injury list is growing, with France's Romain Ntamack expected to be out until the New Year after dislocating his shoulder against Fiji. No timeframe has been set for Mallia's recovery, but reports in France suggest Toulouse could bring in a medical joker if the injury proves serious.

Rugby.title: New World Rugby rankings announced as global game split into three tiers
Rugby.summary: New World Rugby rankings announced as global game split into three tiers Wales Online
bullets: The first round of the Nations Championship autumn leg has shaped the World Rugby rankings, with South Africa remaining number one after a 66-7 win over Italy in Rome. New Zealand beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield, and Ireland, the third-ranked side, beat Argentina 42-12. England's 45-22 win over Australia produced the biggest rankings gain, 1.31 points, taking them close to fourth-placed France, who beat Fiji.

Wales' 28-21 win over Japan moved them further ahead of Italy and Japan and within 0.42 ranking points of ninth-placed Fiji. Next weekend, France host South Africa, Wales play New Zealand, England face Japan, Ireland meet Fiji, Scotland play Australia and Italy host Argentina. Wales' fixture against seventh-placed Australia is viewed as a target for breaking into the top eight.
Rugby.copy:
The first round of the Nations Championship's autumn leg has reaffirmed the huge divide that currently exists in the world game. South Africa's 66-7 demolition of Italy in Rome underlined their status as the world's number one side, showing the gulf in class between the elite and teams further down the pecking order.

Likewise, New Zealand's comfortable 43-21 win over Scotland at Murrayfield proved the two southern hemisphere giants remain a level above the challenging pack in the second tier of teams between fifth and eighth in the rankings table.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock powers seven-try England to crushing victory against Australia
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock powers seven-try England to crushing victory against Australia The Guardian
bullets: England beat Australia with seven tries in their Nations Championship match, scoring a record number of points against the Wallabies. Henry Pollock scored two tries after replacing Manny Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time, with others from Jamie George, Ollie Chessum, Joe Heyes, Jack van Poortvliet and Ben Spencer. Australia's tries came from Max Jorgensen, Filipo Daugunu and Jeremy Williams.

Angus Bell was shown a yellow card for an illegal tackle on Feyi-Waboso, who was later seen in a medical boot, and England scored soon after. They face Japan and New Zealand over the next two Saturdays and could still reach the Nations Championship final at home at the end of the month. The result follows a Six Nations campaign that put Steve Borthwick's regime under pressure.
Rugby.copy:
England had promised to do their talking on the field and so it came to pass. After a turbulent few days, this result was certainly a thumping riposte to newspaper reports that all is not well within the court of Steve Borthwick. If Australia had imagined they might encounter distracted, half-hearted hosts, this seven-try romp suggested the precise opposite.

Maybe Borthwick should commission the Times to write his motivational pre-match speeches every week. On this evidence the Wallabies have some massive issues to address but, equally, England were comfortably the better, more energetic side. Further improvement will still be demanded, of course, but this record number of points against Australia was easily their most satisfying all-round outing of the calendar year to date. Their three defining Ds – defence, discipline and desire – were conspicuous throughout and, at long last, they are starting to trust their exciting attacking talent out wide.

bullets: Eben Etzebeth has been recalled to the Springboks squad for the Nations Championship after uncapped fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed, 20, withdrew from the touring party with a shoulder problem. The 147-Test lock had originally been ruled out through injury but has recovered sufficiently to rejoin the group, and is expected to link up with the squad in France on Monday.

Ahmed, one of six uncapped players selected, missed most of the build-up to Saturday's 66-7 victory over Italy in Turin and will return to South Africa to recover. Rugby.title: New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade at Murrayfield
Rugby.summary: New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade at Murrayfield BBC
bullets: New Zealand beat Scotland by seven tries to three at Murrayfield in the Nations Championship, despite a first-half hat-trick from Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman. Wallace Sititi, Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor, Beauden Barrett (twice), Josh Moorby and Asafo Aumua scored the All Blacks' tries, and only three points separated the sides at half-time.

The All Blacks dominated the second half, scoring 19 unanswered points to lead 43-21 after 50 minutes. Both sides had players sin-binned, with Peter Lakai and Sititi for New Zealand and captain Sione Tuipulotu for Scotland. It was the 34th Test between the nations, with New Zealand now holding 32 wins and two draws since 1905.
Rugby.copy:
Ruthless New Zealand blew Scotland away in a high-class, seven tries to three Nations Championship victory at Murrayfield. Despite a historic first-half hat-trick from Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman, the All Blacks were mostly magnificent, unrelenting and classy. It was the 34th Test between the nations and New Zealand's tally has yet another win - 32 now, with two draws going back to 1905.

Wallace Sititi scored early in a breathless first half. Ashman responded. Ethan de Groot and Codie Taylor hit back to make it 17-7 at the end of the first quarter. New Zealand's Peter Lakai was binned and Ashman got his second while he was off. The sensational Beauden Barrett scored the first of his double straight after. Then, as the bonkerdom stretched on, Sititi was yellow-carded and Ashman made the All Blacks pay with his hat-trick try.

bullets: South Africa beat Italy 66-7 in Turin to maintain their perfect Nations Championship record, scoring nine tries and leading 45-0 at half-time. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu opened the scoring with a penalty and a try, Malcolm Marx scored two maul tries, and Morne van den Berg, Siya Kolisi, Damian Willemse, Wilco Louw, Paul de Villiers and Ethan Hooker also crossed.

The win gives South Africa 20 points from 20 in the Southern Hemisphere table, 89 points clear of New Zealand on points difference. The All Blacks are second on 15 points ahead of their meeting with Scotland at Murrayfield. Federico Ruzza scored Italy's only try, and South Africa next face France and Ireland.
Rugby.copy:
South Africa maintained their perfect Nations Championship record with a brutal 66-7 demolition of injury-hit Italy in Turin, effectively ending the contest before half-time. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu opened the scoring with an early penalty before slicing through from 40 metres for the first of nine Springbok tries, setting the tone for a remarkable opening period.

Morne van den Berg burrowed over from close range before Malcolm Marx crossed from a driving maul. Siya Kolisi followed after Feinberg-Mngomezulu produced a 50:22, before Damian Willemse finished a Jasper Wiese break beneath the posts.

Rugby.title: Keenan hat-trick as six-try Ireland beat Pumas
Rugby.summary: Hugo Keenan scores a hat-trick of tries as Ireland open the home leg of the Nations Championship with a commanding bonus-point win over Argentina in Dublin.
bullets: Hugo Keenan scored a hat-trick as Ireland opened the home leg of the Nations Championship with a six-try, bonus-point win over Argentina in Dublin, finishing 30 points clear. Captain Dan Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Ronan Kelleher also scored, while Mateo Carreras crossed twice for the Pumas.

Ireland move top of the northern hemisphere table and host Fiji next week, before world champions South Africa visit Dublin on 21 November. Andy Farrell has an injury list including Sean Jansen, Rob Baloucoune, Mack Hansen and Josh van der Flier, and Sheehan failed a head injury assessment. Argentina, still without an away win over Ireland in 12 attempts, lost captain Julian Montoya to a failed assessment and next travel to Italy and France.
Rugby.copy:
Hugo Keenan scored a hat-trick of tries as Ireland opened the home leg of the Nations Championship with a commanding bonus-point win over Argentina in Dublin. In addition to Keenan, captain Dan Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Ronan Kelleher crossed as Andy Farrell's side punished a messy and ill-disciplined Pumas outfit, who scored twice through wing Mateo Carreras.

On a deeply disappointing night for Argentina, who are still without an away win over Ireland after 12 attempts, Justo Piccardo and Ephraim Elias were sin-binned while they lost captain Julian Montoya to a failed head injury assessment before half-time.

The double World Cup winner, 35, will miss the Cheetahs' debut at their new European home ground, the round two fixture against Dragons at St Helen's in Swansea on 13 December. The 24-year-old is joined in the England XV by flanker Ben Curry, who makes his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months. Curry, whose twin brother Tom had an injury setback in training earlier this week that took him out of contention, is seen as key to combating Australia's breakdown specialists Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano and ensuring a supply of quick ball to Smith and his backline.

bullets: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has said the sudden death of the team's security chief, Logan Cadwallader, has "rocked" the squad. Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend also paid tribute, saying he did not expect the events of the week to change how the All Blacks play and that Scotland expect one of their best performances. Rugby.title: Money-making Nations Championship project carries a cost for fans and players
Rugby.summary: Money-making Nations Championship project carries a cost for fans and players The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
It was a loose kick, tumbling aimlessly end over end into the All Blacks’ half. Their wing Billy Wallace gathered it and sprinted into midfield, through a gap and on into the Welsh half, only their full-back ahead of him now, and with his teammate Bob Deans in the corner of his eye, coming on the inside calling for the ball. Wallace gave the pass and Deans was away, making straight for the posts, tackled at the last moment by Rhys Gabe, and the two of them went sliding for the try‑line together. The ball finished in the tips of Deans’s fingers, at the end of his outstretched arm.

Over the line? On the line? Inches away from the line? No one knows. The referee John Dewar Dallas insisted that Deans never made it. The match finished 3-0 to Wales: the All Blacks’ solitary defeat in 35 games on their 1905 autumn tour of Europe. Lloyd Jones wrote a great novel about that tour, Carl Nixon turned it into a successful play, Nigel Wray paid £180,000 for the jersey the All Blacks captain Dave Gallaher wore on the day. You can still buy a DVD of a “dramatic reconstruction” of the match, and a century later two Kiwi journalists published a book offering what they considered new, definitive proof about what happened.

bullets: Captain Sione Tuipulotu and fly-half Finn Russell return to Scotland's starting XV for Saturday's Test against New Zealand, as the Scots seek a first win over the All Blacks in their 34th meeting. It is the first of four Tests this month, with Australia and Japan also visiting Edinburgh. Rugby.copy:

"They're playing some excellent rugby right now and it's our first game of the season, which is always the toughest challenge for us too," head coach Townsend said. "It's great we now get this opportunity to play New Zealand again. It's a different New Zealand team.

bullets: The Rugby Football Union has said it will keep Steve Borthwick as England head coach through his contract, whatever the results between now and the World Cup. His deal was extended two months ago until after the 2028 Six Nations, despite England's worst Six Nations performance, which included four defeats and a first-ever loss to Italy. RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney said the union is committed to him and wants to see continued progress.

England face Australia at Allianz Stadium on Sunday in the Nations Championship, then play Japan and New Zealand this autumn before the finals weekend at Twickenham. Sweeney said ticket sales for the two finals on Friday 27 November have been sluggish, while Saturday and Sunday are more encouraging. He said the extension was meant to remove uncertainty for the coaching team going into the 2027 World Cup in Australia, and that succession planning is looked at continually.
Rugby.copy:
Steve Borthwick enters England’s autumn campaign with the backing of the Rugby Football Union to see out his contract whatever the results between now and the World Cup. Borthwick’s reign as head coach was extended until after the 2028 Six Nations two months ago, even though earlier this year England had crashed to their worst performance in the tournament’s history.

Victories against Fiji and Argentina during a July tour that opened with a comprehensive loss to South Africa eased the pressure on Borthwick, who is currently preparing his team for Sunday’s Nations Championship clash with Australia at Allianz Stadium.

Rugby.title: Six Nations and Sanzaar agree to sell global broadcast rights together in unique deal
Rugby.summary: Six Nations and Sanzaar agree to sell global broadcast rights together in unique deal The Guardian
bullets: The Six Nations and Sanzaar unions have agreed to sell all their media rights and commercial deals collectively for the first time, under a new revenue-sharing model described as the first of its kind in sport. Southern hemisphere nations will share in profits from the Six Nations and British & Irish Lions tours, while European countries will benefit from deals generated by the Rugby Championship and the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series between New Zealand and South Africa.

A new rights management agency, set up by the 10-person board running the Nations Championship, will manage sales. The new arrangements are expected to affect sponsorship and commercial deals from 2028, but not TV rights until 2030, as existing Six Nations and Sanzaar broadcast rights run to 2029. From 2030 the Six Nations, Rugby Championship and Nations Championship will be sold together, with bespoke packages also available. RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney said the aim is a more efficient approach to the market and higher overall valuations.
Rugby.copy:
The Six Nations and Sanzaar unions have agreed to sell all their media rights and commercial deals collectively for the first time in a new revenue-sharing model. In an innovative arrangement that is the first of its kind in sport, the southern hemisphere nations will receive a share of the profits generated by the Six Nations and British & Irish Lions tours, while the European countries will benefit from broadcast and sponsorship deals generated by the Rugby Championship and the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series between New Zealand and South Africa.

The sales process will be managed by a new rights management agency to be set up by a 10-person board that has been created to run the Nations Championship, which resumes this weekend.

Rugby.copy:
The 13th team participating at the Nations Championship this month are an intriguing bunch. If you didn’t know much about rugby and had wandered into a first-floor conference room at a hotel near Windsor on Monday you might almost have mistaken them for a gathering of airline pilots from nearby Heathrow. Slim, intelligent, studious … you’d trust them to stay calm on the flight deck.

Stick them in matchday kit, however, and the world’s top rugby union referees do not always enjoy universal respect, certainly online. They can be unflappably brilliant for 79 and a half minutes and yet still be defined by one hairline call barely visible to the naked eye. Every Test in which they are involved is an away game and, popularity wise, they often receive the same unconditional love as traffic wardens and the chancellor of the exchequer.

Racket.summary: Jannik Sinner: World No 2 confirms aim to return to tennis at Australian Open after lengthy absence with knee injury Sky Sports
bullets: Jannik Sinner has confirmed he aims to return at the Australian Open in January, having not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July because of a knee injury. The 25-year-old, who has lost the world No 1 ranking to Alexander Zverev, won the Melbourne title in 2024 and 2025 and lost to Novak Djokovic in this year's semi-final. Speaking at a press conference in Milan, he said he may play a few earlier tournaments but would take recovery one step at a time.

Sinner thanked Jack Draper, Matteo Berrettini and Carlos Alcaraz for their support during his injury absence. Draper has ruled out a return before 2027. Sinner parted ways with coach Darren Cahill last week after four years, and Sweden's Magnus Norman has joined his team, with Simone Vagnozzi remaining for continuity. Sinner also congratulated Kimi Antonelli, 20, on becoming the youngest Formula 1 world champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

bullets: World No. 1 Ahn Se-young beat Japan's world No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi 21-12, 15-21, 21-16 in the women's singles final of the BWF World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) in Yeosu on 8 November. It was her first Korea Open title since 2023 and avenged her loss to Yamaguchi in last year's final. It was her 11th title of the season, making her the first player to win 11 in two consecutive years.

Ahn has a 71-1 record this season and a 55-match winning streak since losing to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. Susi Susanti's record of 59 consecutive wins stands from 1993 to 1994. Can she achieve her second win in Kumamoto after two years? She has recently competed in major tournaments and is currently in the process of regaining her form. Racket.title: How prize money and ranking points will be awarded at the 2026 WTA Finals
Racket.summary: Prize money is down from 12 months ago, but big ranking points are still on offer. The post How prize money and ranking points will be awarded at the 2026 WTA Finals appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The winner of the 2026 WTA Finals in Indian Wells can earn up to 1,500 ranking points, the most available outside the four Grand Slams, after year-end world No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew with a viral illness. Players earn 200 points for each round-robin win, 400 for a semi-final win and 500 for the final, with no points awarded for qualifying.

The total prize money pool is $10m across singles and doubles, down 35.5% from $15.25m in Riyadh last season. Each singles player receives a $220,000 participation fee plus $230,000 per round-robin win. Semi-final winners earn a further $820,000 and the champion $1.64m, so an unbeaten champion would take home about $3.37m.
Racket.copy:
The 2026 WTA Tour season is coming to a close, but for eight singles players there is one more task at hand: the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The tournament was dealt a significant blow on Saturday with Elena Rybakina, the year-end world No 1 and defending WTA Finals champion, forced to withdraw from the championships due to a viral illness.

However, action is still set to get underway to a strong start on Sunday, with Marta Kostyuk — Rybakina’s replacement — set to face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the opening singles match, before 2024 WTA Finals champion Coco Gauff faces Jessica Pegula later in the day.

bullets: An Se Young won the Korea Open 2026 in Yeosu, beating Akane Yamaguchi 21-12 15-21 21-16 in the women's singles final in front of a packed Jinnam Stadium. It was her 11th title of the year, equalling her own 2025 total and leaving her one short of a new record for most titles in a single year across all badminton disciplines.

An and Yamaguchi have met 40 times, and Yamaguchi won last year's Korea Open final, though An has now won 11 matches in a row. She described playing in front of Korean fans, which is rare for her, as feeling like a dream, and said tough matches against top players make her more stable.
Racket.copy:
A well deserved crown on her head, An Se Young has matched her own greatest season. Her win at the YEOSU VICTOR Korea Open 2026 is her 11th title of the year, equalling the tally she set in 2025 and leaving her one crown away from a new benchmark for the most titles won in a single year across all badminton disciplines. A remarkable achievement.

And she did it in style on home soil. A rare appearance in front of a packed Jinnam Stadium in Yeosu became a celebration as two titans of the sport went head-to-head when An outlasted Akane Yamaguchi 21-12 15-21 21-16 to seal the title.

Racket.title: Badminton star An Se-young wins Korea Open for record-tying 11th int'l title
Racket.summary: Badminton star An Se-young wins Korea Open for record-tying 11th int'l title The Korea Times
bullets: South Korea's An Se-young won the women's singles at the Yeosu Victor Korea Open on Sunday, beating Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21-12, 15-21, 21-16 at Jinnam Stadium. The world No. 1 claimed her 11th international title of the year, tying the record set by Kento Momota in 2019 and equalled by An herself in 2025. The Korea Open is the only Korean event on the BWF World Tour.

An has won eight World Tour tournaments this year, plus gold at the Badminton Asia Championships, the BWF World Championships and the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. She has lost only once in 72 matches, to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. She will now rest before the BWF World Tour Finals, which start on 9 December in Hangzhou, China.
Racket.copy:
Korean badminton star An Se-young won her record-tying 11th international title of the year on home soil Sunday. An, world No. 1, defeated second-ranked Akane Yamaguchi of Japan 2-1 (21-12, 15-21, 21-16) in the women's singles final at Yeosu Victor Korea Open at Jinnam Stadium in Yeosu, some 320 kilometers southwest of Seoul.

The Korea Open is the only Korean event on the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour. This was An's 11th international victory of the year, tying the record first set by the men's singles player Kento Momota in 2019 and equaled by An herself in 2025.

Racket.summary: Carlos Alcaraz says he is ready for "one of most difficult challenges in tennis" after setting up a rematch against Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final.
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz reached the Paris Masters final with a 6-4 6-4 win over Casper Ruud in 86 minutes, and will face Ben Shelton in a rematch of their US Open quarter-final. The 23-year-old world number three had escaped two match points to beat Taylor Fritz in the previous round. He won 86% of points on his first serve and 11 of 13 points at the net.

Shelton, the world number four, beat Frenchman Luca van Assche 5-7 6-3 6-4 to become the first American men's singles finalist in Paris since 2017. He ended Alcaraz's US Open title defence in a five-set match that finished at 03:34 local time. Alcaraz, who returned from a four-month wrist injury layoff at that tournament, is on an eight-match winning streak after winning in Vienna last week.

Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament.

But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Racket.title: Jannik Sinner: Coach Darren Cahill to leave Italian's side at end of 2026
Racket.summary: Jannik Sinner: Coach Darren Cahill to leave Italian's side at end of 2026 BBC
bullets: Darren Cahill will leave Jannik Sinner's coaching team at the end of 2026. The 61-year-old Australian joined in June 2022, when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10, and with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi helped him win five Grand Slams and spend 95 weeks as world number one. Swede Magnus Norman, long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join the team next season.

Sinner, 25, has not played since winning Wimbledon for a second year in a row in July because of injury, and Alexander Zverev has recently overtaken him at the top of the rankings. He is set to return at the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia next month. Cahill had planned to leave at the end of 2025 but told Sinner at Wimbledon he could stay if he won the title. Sinner said Cahill helped him grow as a player and as a person.

Racket.summary: A smaller prize pot after leaving Saudi Arabia. The post WTA Finals prize money slashed by £4m as 2026 Indian Wells alternates confirmed appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The WTA Finals prize pot has fallen to $10m (£7.42m) for the 2026 edition at Indian Wells, a drop of $5.5m (£4m) from the $15.5m (£11.5m) offered in Riyadh last year. An undefeated singles champion will earn $3.37m (£2.5m) including participation fees, compared with the $5.23m (£3.8m) Elena Rybakina received in 2025. Singles has $8m of the total and doubles $2m, with the winning pair able to earn $725,000 (£538,480).

Each singles player receives $220,000 (£163,379) for taking part and $230,000 (£170,877) for each round-robin win. That rises to $820,000 (£609,214) for a semi-final win and $1.64m (£1.21m) for the title, and an undefeated champion collects 1,500 ranking points. Marta Kostyuk and Diana Shnaider are the alternates, while Iga Swiatek chose not to be one after ending her season with a left thigh injury.
Racket.copy:
The WTA have revealed there will be a significant drop in prize money from last year’s WTA Finals to the 2026 edition in Indian Wells. In 2025, Elena Rybakina went undefeated as she won the title in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, but this year, the season-ending tournament has moved away from the Middle East.

Over the summer, it was announced that Indian Wells would host the season finale, which includes world No 1 Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, among others.

Emma Raducanu recently gave fans a glimpse of her recovery journey with videos of her gym routine, suggesting she is making progress ahead of the new season. Raducanu slipped and strained her left thigh in the Queen's Club quarter-final, and during her run to the final she aggravated a pre-existing right shin problem, which was later diagnosed as a grade-four stress fracture. The injury forced her to withdraw from the Wimbledon Championships at the last moment and later ruled her out of the US Open and the Asian swing. It kept her off the court for the rest of her 2026 season. Months after navigating the pain and recovery process, Raducanu was recently seen taking off her medical walking boot and resuming light training at the National Tennis Centre in London.

She was seen doing a few jump variations and hitting a few shots on court. Sharing glimpses of her recent training sessions, she wrote: Raducanu's 2026 season faced multiple setbacks, including her second-round loss at the Australian Open. It is only the second time in 20 seasons that he has failed to qualify when fit. He likely needed a semi-final place in Paris, and said his plan for the next few weeks is "just rest".

Only Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul remain in contention for the final two places, currently held by Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar. Tiafoe lost to Quentin Halys and Alex de Minaur to Tomas Martin Etcheverry. World number one Alexander Zverev and Daniil Medvedev, both already qualified, were also beaten. Djokovic reached the Australian Open final and Wimbledon semi-finals this year but has not reached a Masters 1000 quarter-final.

Racket.title: Hampstead’s Dart crazy WTA Tour single title win at 2026 Guangzhou Open
Racket.summary: Hampstead’s Dart crazy WTA Tour single title win at 2026 Guangzhou Open Hackney Gazette
Racket.copy:
Hampstead tennis ace Harriet Dart celebrated her crazy week at 2026 Guangzhou Open claiming her first WTA Tour singles title, writes Ziad Chaudry. The 30-year-old defeated Austria’s up-and-coming teenage sensation Lilli Tagger, ranked number 53 on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz world rankings, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in two hours and 18 minutes on the hardcourts of Nansha International Tennis Centre, Guangzhou, China to scoop the $37,390 (£27,700) winners’ cheque along with lifting the plate-type trophy.

Dart’s journey to being champion in this WTA250-ranked event began in the first qualifying round beating Hong Kong’s Cheuk Ying Shek 5-7, 7-6(5), 6-1. After easily disposing Mei Yamaguchi from Japan 6-2, 6-1 in the final qualifying round, the GB Billie Jean King Cup regular disposed Russia’s Tatiana Prozorova (6-4, 2-6, 6-2), world-ranked 46 Janice Tjen of Indonesia (6-4, 3-6, 6-3), Spain’s former world number two Paula Badosa (3-6, 6-2, 6-4) and Chinese home favourite Sun Xinran (5-7, 7-6(1), 6-0) before defeating Tagger, the 2025 Roland Garros junior girls singles champion Tagger and this year’s Livesport Prague Open WTA 250 event winner, in the final.

Racket.title: GB's Stojsavljevic, 17, claims first WTA Tour win despite short notice
Racket.summary: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beats former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin for her first WTA Tour main-draw win.
bullets: British 17-year-old Mika Stojsavljevic claimed her first WTA Tour main-draw win by beating former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin 6-3 4-6 6-4 at the Hong Kong Open. The world number 411 lost in qualifying but entered the main draw as a lucky loser, and had only an hour's notice that she would be playing. She will face world number 67 Zeynep Sonmez in the second round.

Stojsavljevic became the first Briton in 15 years to win the US Open junior title in 2024 and turned professional in 2025. Earlier this year she beat then world number 56 Talia Gibson in Billie Jean King Cup qualifying in April and reached the quarter-finals of the WTA 125 event in Birmingham. Fellow Briton Katie Boulter's season ended with a 7-5 6-4 loss to American Claire Liu at the same tournament.

Racket.title: P.V. Sindhu qualifies for 2026 BWF World Tour Finals
Racket.summary: P.V. Sindhu qualifies for 2026 BWF World Tour Finals Sportstar
bullets: India's P.V. Sindhu has qualified for the BWF World Tour Finals, the Badminton World Federation confirmed on Wednesday. It is the 31-year-old's sixth appearance at the event and her first since 2021. She qualified in 2022 but withdrew through injury. The tournament takes place in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December. An Se Young, Akane Yamaguchi, Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei have also secured places.

Sindhu won the Hylo Open in Germany last week and is likely to play next at the Syed Modi International in Lucknow, which starts on 24 November. She remains the only Indian to win the women's singles title at the World Tour Finals, having beaten Japan's Nozomi Okuhara in the 2018 final.
Racket.copy:
India’s P.V. Sindhu has qualified for the year-ender BWF World Tour Finals, Badminton World Federation confirmed on Wednesday. This is the 31-year-old’s sixth career appearance in the World Tour Finals and her first since 2021. She had qualified for 2022 but withdrew due to an injury.

The World Tour Finals will take place in Hangzhou, China, from December 9-13. An Se Young, Akane Yamaguchi, Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei are the others who have sealed their berths.

Racket.title: 2026 WTA Finals draw: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Coco Gauff, Linda Noskova find out groups
Racket.summary: Which WTA Finals group is tougher? The post 2026 WTA Finals draw: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Coco Gauff, Linda Noskova find out groups appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The 2026 WTA Finals draw has placed world number one and defending champion Elena Rybakina in Group 1 with No 4 Coco Gauff, No 5 Jessica Pegula and No 8 Linda Noskova. World number two Aryna Sabalenka heads Group 2 alongside No 3 Mirra Andreeva, No 6 Elina Svitolina and No 7 Karolina Muchova. Rybakina is top seed for the first time, and the pair can only meet in the semi-finals or final.

The tournament has moved from Riyadh to the Indian Wells Tennis Garden in California. It starts on Sunday 8 November, with the final on 15 November. Rybakina opens against Noskova, whom she leads 3-0 head-to-head. Noskova, Andreeva and Muchova are making their WTA Finals debuts. Marta Kostyuk and Diana Shnaider are the alternates. Rybakina won last year's title unbeaten, beating Sabalenka in the final.
Racket.copy:
The 2026 WTA Finals draw is out and world No 1 Elena Rybakina appears to have a tough draw in Group 1, whereas Aryna Sabalenka’s group is probably more evenly matched. Defending champion Rybakina is the top seed at the season-ending tournament for the first time following her rise to the top of both the WTA Rankings and Race To Indian Wells.

World No 2 Sabalenka – who has been the top seed the past three years – headlines Group 2 so they can only face each other in either the semi-final or the final. Reigning Australian Open and US Open champion Rybakina has ended up with world No 4 Coco Gauff, No 5 Jessica Pegula and No 8 Linda Noskova in Group A while Sabalenka will face No 3 Mirra Andreeva, No 6 Elina Svitolina and No 7 Karolina Muchova.

Golf.title: LIV Golf seeks Chapter 11 protection amid planned 2027 relaunch
Golf.summary: LIV Golf seeks Chapter 11 protection amid planned 2027 relaunch Financier Worldwide
bullets: LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey, as part of a restructuring support agreement with UK private equity firm BC Partners Credit. The petition lists liabilities of $500m to $1bn and assets of $100m to $500m. The Public Investment Fund has agreed to provide $49.6m in debtor-in-possession financing during the court-supervised process, and BC Partners Credit and minority investors are expected to act as plan sponsors and provide exit financing.

The league intends to resume global team-based competition in 2027 under a revised ownership structure, subject to court approval and stakeholder support, and recent filings indicate players could hold a majority stake. The PIF said in April that it would stop funding the league after investing more than $5bn, and at least $45m is believed to be owed to players. Chief executive Scott O'Neil said the process gives the league time to pursue a transaction built around fans and a player-first ownership model.
Golf.copy:
Controversial breakaway golf league LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey as part of a restructuring agreement with UK private equity firm BC Partners that it hopes will secure the league’s future beyond 2026.

The organisation, which created significant division within professional golf following its launch in 2022, reported liabilities of between $500m and $1bn and assets of between $100m and $500m in its Chapter 11 petition.

Golf.title: Brown, 19, becomes youngest PGA winner in 95 years
Golf.summary: Teenager Blades Brown beats Ben James at the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico to become the youngest PGA Tour tournament winner since 1938.
bullets: Nineteen-year-old Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years by taking the World Wide Technology Championship in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. He beat fellow American Ben James on the second play-off hole after a nine-under-par 63, including a birdie on the 18th, to come from seven shots behind. Both finished on 23 under, with Michael Kim third on 22 under.

At 19 years and 171 days, Brown is the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis, 18, won the 1931 Michigan Open. He is the first teenage winner since Jordan Spieth won the 2013 John Deere Classic at 19 years and 352 days. Brown turned professional at 17 and secured his PGA Tour card by finishing in the top 20 of the Korn Ferry Tour points list earlier this year. He said the magnitude of the win had not yet set in.
Golf.copy:
Nineteen-year-old Blades Brown became the youngest winner on the PGA Tour in 95 years with a thrilling victory in the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico. Brown beat fellow American Ben James on the second play-off hole in Cabo San Lucas after shooting a nine-under-par 63, which included a birdie on the 18th, to come from seven shots behind.

At 19 years and 171 days, he is the youngest PGA winner since 18-year-old Charles Kocsis won the 1931 Michigan Open, which was considered a regional event in the early years of the tour.

bullets: BC Partners has quietly revived efforts to create a successor to LIV Golf, a week after abandoning its "LIV 2.0" plans, according to the Financial Times. The private equity firm is exploring the purchase of a $50m bankruptcy loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), which would give it greater control over establishing a new league. LIV filed for bankruptcy in September after PIF, previously a 98% stakeholder, withdrew its financial backing.

BC Partners had committed $300m to a proposed successor of up to 17 tournaments, but the plan reportedly collapsed over player financial guarantees. It believes PGA Tour schedule changes from 2028 and the DP World Tour's financial difficulties could leave room for a team-based rival. Bryson DeChambeau said he "gave everything" to keep team golf alive and will play the Nedbank Golf Challenge next month. Golf.summary: While Rory McIlroy and others are willing to welcome LIV defectors back to the PGA Tour, not everyone has the same feeling. "Go to Q school." The post LIV Golf’s end brought harsh answers to the sport’s most pressing question appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Facing what would become golf’s biggest question, Xander Schauffele said he wasn’t sure where he stood. Jon Rahm’s attorney had just announced his client’s departure from LIV Golf, and Schauffele, one of the faces of the PGA Tour, was asked about a road back for defectors like Rahm. He didn’t divulge his feelings on the matter, but his explanation for the obstacles ahead once the LIV threat officially ended would prove prescient one month later.

“I’ve got no idea,” Schauffele said at the Baycurrent Classic last month. “There are 225 guys with Tour cards and if you sat down and interviewed all of them, you’re going to get probably three or four boxes of how guys feel. Some guys don’t care, some guys are really ticked off, some guys want them to have a huge fine, some guys would let them back tomorrow. Where I stand in those boxes, I don’t really know. I’m in the sort of, I try to mind my own business most times.”

Golf.copy:
Ryder Cup team-mates Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton reeled in Francesco Laporta to share the lead heading into the weekend at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Italian Laporta had led after a brilliant 62 on day one but a 70 in round two at Yas Links left the door ajar and close friends Hatton and Rahm took advantage.

Hatton carded a 65, two shots fewer than Rahm, and the pair will now both head into the weekend at 12 under alongside Laporta looking for a record sixth Rolex Series victory. Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau Dealt Great News After LIV Golf Shutdown Heavy.com
bullets: Bryson DeChambeau has been offered full DP World Tour playing privileges for 2027, according to The Telegraph, as LIV Golf moves towards liquidation. He qualifies under the Category 1 exemption, which covers major winners and Race to Dubai champions from the past seven years, through his 2024 US Open win at Pinehurst. He must submit his membership application by 14 November and has not confirmed whether he will accept.

LIV's board confirmed an orderly wind-down after the league failed to secure investment for its LIV 2.0 format. BC Partners had considered investing $300m but withdrew after failing to secure commitments from leading players. A top-10 finish on the 2027 Race to Dubai could help DeChambeau regain a PGA Tour card for 2028, though he may face a one-year suspension, as Jon Rahm expects to. Rahm is expected to play the DP World Tour in 2027, with Hatton and Garcia expected to return to Europe.

Not in 21 years and 1,014 rounds on the DP World Tour had Rory McIlroy ever made 11 birdies in a competitive round. But just 24 hours after accepting a two-shot penalty which seemed a significant blow to his hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai, McIlroy conjured another magical personal record as he surged into contention at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy’s 9-under par 63 lit up the second round at Yas Links, a blitz that included seven birdies on the back nine. It all came after taking an unplayable and making bogey on the first, as well as the rules incident that threatened to spoil a solid start to his tournament.

Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy recovers from the setback of being penalised two shots in his opening round at the Abu Dhabi Championship by firing 11 birdies in a nine-under-par 63 in round two on Friday.
bullets: Rory McIlroy carded a nine-under-par 63 in the second round of the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links, making 11 birdies to reach 11 under overall and move within one shot of the lead. Spain's Jon Rahm, England's Tyrrell Hatton and Italy's Francesco Laporta share the lead at 12 under, while McIlroy sits in a four-strong group alongside Sam Bairstow, Matthew Jordan and Adrian Meronk.

McIlroy had finished the first round two under par, eight shots off the lead, after a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on the 12th hole. He said he had "made peace" with the ruling and played with a clear conscience. He is chasing a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title and a record-equalling eighth overall, level with Colin Montgomerie. bullets: Rory McIlroy received a two-shot penalty for improving his lie during the opening round of the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links, after pressing his club on the grass behind his ball before a chip on the par-four 12th. The penalty turned his six into a quadruple-bogey eight and his four-under 68 into a two-under 70, leaving him eight shots behind leader Francesco Laporta.

The DP World Tour said McIlroy breached rule 8.1b(4), which allows a player to ground the club lightly but not press it on the ground. McIlroy said there was no intent but he was happy to take the penalty, as he did not want people to think he had got away with something. He is tied on two under with Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra, while Jon Rahm shot a 65 in his first round since leaving LIV Golf.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has been hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie during the opening round of the Abu Dhabi Championship. The six-time major winner was penalised after pressing down on the grass behind his ball with his club before hitting a chip on the par-four 12th at Yas Links.

In a statement, the DP World Tour said McIlroy had breached rule 8.1b(4), which permits a player "to ground their club lightly right in front of or behind the ball". The statement added: "'Ground the club lightly' means allowing the weight of the club to be supported by the grass on or above the ground surface and there is no penalty even if the lie is improved.

BC Partners had been expected to provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing in April, which led to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September.

An attorney for LIV is expected to tell a court hearing on Thursday that the LIV 2.0 proposal is not viable. The league had announced a 2027 schedule including an Adelaide event at Kooyonga Golf Club from 18-21 March, but South Australia Premier Peter Malinauskas said he did not expect it to go ahead. The PIF spent more than $5bn (£3.7bn) on the league, and the DP World Tour had said players joining LIV next season would not be tour members in 2027.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf is set to be wound down after its investor withdrew support because the proposed new league failed to attract enough players. LIV had hoped BC Partners Credit would provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing in April, leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September.

The funding could have helped the competition move forward in a new form, dubbed LIV 2.0, but BC Partners is understood to have decided it is not viable to pursue a deal. While leading players such as Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia had already walked away, BBC Sport understands that those working on LIV 2.0 had received commitments from co-investors, felt support from within the golf ecosystem and had about 30 players signed up, including major winners.

bullets: Rory McIlroy said at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on Wednesday that a rule on Ryder Cup captaincy persuaded him to keep his DP World Tour membership. He had considered giving it up in 2019 to focus on the United States, but DP World Tour chief executive Keith Pelley told him that anyone who resigned their membership could not be a Ryder Cup captain or vice captain in future.

McIlroy was speaking for the first time since the latest LIV news, and also discussed golf's 'false economy' era and LIV's push towards an 'arms race'. Sergio Garcia, who recently announced he is leaving LIV to join the DP World Tour next season, has said he wants to be part of the Ryder Cup again. The rule has complicated the path for European captains after Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter, Henrik Stenson and others left for LIV. Stenson was stripped of the 2023 captaincy, and Luke Donald took over.
Golf.copy:
When it comes to pre-tournament press conferences, many can sometimes feel repetitive. Some players simply have more to say than others, or there aren’t as many interesting topics or questions for players to opine on.

But at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on Wednesday, Rory McIlroy’s time with the media was one many had circled. Speaking for the first time since the latest batch of LIV news dropped, McIlroy, one of the game’s most outspoken and thoughtful figures, riffed on golf’s “false economy” era, LIV’s desire to turn professional golf into an “arms race” and more.

Golf.copy:
DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings has “delivered a bullish but, at the same time, realistic update on the circuit,” describing the current uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf as a “chance for all of golf to ‘reset,’” according to a Q&A by Martin Dempster of THE SCOTSMAN. Kinnings spoke openly about several key aspects of the tour, “from speculation about the current health of the circuit to the wellbeing of its members and its plans for membership and invites for next season.” Questions and answers have been edited for clarity and brevity.

Q: What are your thoughts on the DP World Tour in the current landscape? Kinnings: “Our financial structure, like any global business, is complicated. … But the reality shows that there is some real strength, some stuff which makes me bullish about now and what we’re going to do going forward. We have strong cash reserves, but the thing that’s most notable for me is our record sponsorship levels. … We’re over 100 per cent up from 2019 to 2025 with over a billion dollars currently contracted across the Tour. … And it’s not just the sponsorship. You’ve got TV viewership up seven per cent this year alongside consumer levels in terms of ticketing and merch and hospitality up 30 per cent year on year. So people are engaged.”

Golf.title: Women's TGL: Sky Sports to show exclusive live coverage of new women's team golf league featuring LPGA Tour stars
Golf.summary: Women's TGL: Sky Sports to show exclusive live coverage of new women's team golf league featuring LPGA Tour stars Sky Sports
bullets: Sky Sports has secured exclusive UK and Ireland rights to the WTGL, the new women's team golf league run in partnership with the LPGA Tour. The inaugural season begins on 8 November, and the 2026 and 2027 competitions will both be shown exclusively live, including the play-offs from 20 to 23 December.

The league is played in a custom-built indoor arena in Florida, with five teams of five players who have 48 combined Solheim Cup appearances and 15 major titles between them. Charley Hull, Lottie Woad and Jeeno Thitikul are among the first players. The deal is part of an expansion of Sky's golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi. The men's league grows to seven teams in 2027, and its third season starts on 27 December.
Golf.copy:
Sky Sports has secured exclusive rights in the UK and Ireland to the WTGL, the new women’s team golf league in partnership with the LPGA Tour. Beginning on November 8, the inaugural WTGL season will bring the innovative team golf format - played in a custom-built indoor arena in Florida - to the women's game.

Both the 2026 and 2027 competitions will be broadcast exclusively on Sky Sports as part of an expansion of its golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi.

Golf.title: Patrick Reed happy to be chasing Race to Dubai glory in the desert - Articles - Rolex Series
Golf.summary: Patrick Reed happy to be chasing Race to Dubai glory in the desert - Articles - Rolex Series DP World Tour
Golf.copy:
Patrick Reed returns to the desert this week confident he can rediscover his early season form and become just the second American to be crowned Europe's Number One. The 2018 Masters winner enjoyed a stunning International Swing in the Middle East in January and February, winning a maiden Rolex Series title at the Dubai Desert Classic, losing in a play-off at the Bapco Energies Bahrain Championship and then winning the Qatar Masters in consecutive weeks.

That catapulted him to the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World and there he sat for most of the season until Eugenio Chacarra's third victory of the campaign at last month's DP World India Championship saw the Spaniard replace him.

Golf.title: American Korda wins LPGA Tour player of the year
Golf.summary: World number one Nelly Korda claims her second points-based LPGA player-of-the-year award.
bullets: World number one Nelly Korda has won her second points-based LPGA player-of-the-year award, having first won it in 2024. The 28-year-old won four times in 2026, including the Chevron Championship and the US Women's Open at Riviera, and secured the award with three tournaments remaining.

Korda is on 26 points and one victory away from qualifying for the LPGA Hall of Fame, which requires 27 points plus a mandatory performance requirement. A major win is worth two points and a tour victory one. Rivals Haeran Ryu, who also won two majors, withdrew from last week's event in Malaysia injured, while Miyu Yamashita and Jeeno Thitikul are not entering The Annika. Lydia Ko and Inbee Park were both 27 when they qualified for the Hall of Fame.
Golf.copy:
World number one Nelly Korda has claimed her second points-based LPGA player-of-the-year award. The 28-year-old won four times this year, including the first two majors - The Chevron Championship and the US Women's Open at Riviera.

The American, who won the award in 2024, is one victory away from qualifying for the LPGA Hall of Fame. To qualify for the Hall of Fame, a player must accumulate 27 points and meet a mandatory performance requirement.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy makes remarkable admission about ‘ironic’ LIV Golf
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy makes remarkable admission about ‘ironic’ LIV Golf bunkered.co.uk
bullets: Rory McIlroy has backed DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings' claim that LIV Golf officials said at Augusta this year that they wanted to destroy the European Tour. Speaking before the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, McIlroy said the comments were made verbatim. He called it ironic that LIV now talks of completing rather than competing. Kinnings had told The Scotsman the tour must protect itself from an entity that has spent over $7bn.

McIlroy said the DP World Tour is as strong as it has been in a long time. He said a new agreement with the PGA Tour beyond 2027 is progressing and could be finalised within weeks. He believes LIV gave players too much leverage and created a false economy. McIlroy trails Patrick Reed by around 300 points and Eugenio Chacarra by around 1,000 in the Race to Dubai. He is bidding for a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit title.
Golf.copy:

Rory McIlroy has claimed that officials from the LIV Golf league were insisting they wanted to destroy the European Tour whilst at The Masters earlier this year.

McIlroy, speaking ahead of this week’s Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, defended DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings, who made the same revelation in an interview with The Scotsman.

Golf.title: PGA Tour Champions Stars Excited By Tiger Woods Talk But Big Split Over LIV Golfers
Golf.summary: PGA Tour Champions Stars Excited By Tiger Woods Talk But Big Split Over LIV Golfers Golf Monthly
bullets: Tiger Woods is seriously considering playing on the PGA Tour Champions next season, according to two-time season champion Steven Alker. Alker said the talk in the locker room is that the 50-year-old wants to play big events such as the invitationals and the US Senior Open, where a win would give him a record 10th USGA title, ahead of Bobby Jones.

The tour's membership is divided over whether LIV Golf players should be allowed to return. Alker called it a Catch-22 between raising the tour's profile and opposition from some members. He said the PAC board has discussed whether the PGA Tour's suspension rules, which ranged from six months to a year, should apply. The circuit has lost its PGA Tour pension payments and recognises that big names can bring extra sponsorship. The season ends at the Charles Schwab Cup Championship next week.
Golf.copy:
Tiger Woods is seriously considering playing on the PGA Tour Champions next season, and while he'd be a welcome addition to the senior circuit the prospect of veteran LIV Golf stars returning has the playing membership divided.

The current season comes to a climax at the Charles Schwab Cup Championship next week, but it's the 2027 campaign that's the talk of the town among the seniors with two huge topics on the agenda.

Golf.title: Lucas Herbert Reveals Major Reason For LIV Golf Exit
Golf.summary: Lucas Herbert Reveals Major Reason For LIV Golf Exit Golf Monthly
Golf.copy:
Lucas Herbert says a lack of both quantity and quality events on the proposed LIV Golf 2.0 was a big reason behind him turning his back on the team tour and heading back to the DP World Tour.

On top of that, though, his desire to get into and shine in the Majors more often prompted his decision to join the ranks of players ruling out signing up for LIV Golf 2.0. Herbert finished fourth on the LIV Golf standings after two wins last season, but still decided that his future lies away from the team-based tour and away from the all-Australian Ripper GC.
